props.label: About Us
props.heading: A jeweller Nagpur families keep coming back to
props.body:
Karande Jewellers is a family jewellery house on Jaitala Road in Nagpur, dealing in gold, silver, diamonds and certified gemstones.

We do three things: we sell jewellery, we buy and exchange what you already own, and we advise on gemstones. All of it is done the same way — the piece is weighed in front of you, the rate is the day's rate, and making charges are stated separately so you can see how the figure was reached.

Vijay Karande also consults on astrological gemstones: which stone suits you, at what weight, in which metal and on which finger. That conversation happens before you buy anything, because it often changes what you should be buying.

We are open every day of the week, including Sundays.

props.label: Astrology Consulting
props.heading: The stone first, the purchase after
props.body:
People often buy a gemstone and then ask whether it was the right one. It is worth doing in the other order.

A consultation with Vijay Karande covers which stone suits you, the weight it should be, the metal it should be set in, and which finger it should be worn on. Those four answers change what you should buy — and sometimes the answer is a smaller stone than you were about to purchase.

We hold the consultation before the sale for exactly that reason. It is a better conversation when nobody has paid for anything yet.

props.label: Our Story
props.heading: A legacy of trust
props.body:
A jeweller is not chosen the way an ordinary shop is chosen. Families come back over decades, and they come back for reasons that have very little to do with the window display.

It comes down to whether the weighing is done in front of you, whether the rate you are quoted is the rate everyone gets that day, and whether the answer to "what will you give me for this old chain" is the same on the day you sell as it sounded on the day you bought.

That is what Karande Jewellers is built on, and it is why most of our customers came here because somebody in their family sent them.

posts.excerpt: Why families come back to the same jeweller across generations — and what "trust" actually means when you are buying gold by weight.
posts.body:
A jeweller is not chosen the way a shop is chosen. Families come back over decades, and they come back for reasons that have very little to do with the window display.

It comes down to whether the weighing is done in front of you, whether the rate you are quoted is the rate everyone gets that day, and whether the answer to "what will you give me for this old chain" is the same on the day you sell as it sounded on the day you bought.

That is the whole of it. There is no secret to it and no substitute for having done it the same way for a long time.

posts.title: A Legacy of Gold Jewellery
posts.excerpt: How gold moves through an Indian family — as a wedding gift, as savings, and as something remade for the next generation.
posts.body:
Gold in an Indian household is rarely bought once and worn forever. It is given at a wedding, kept for years, and then at some point brought back to be melted and made into something the next person will actually wear.

That is why weight and purity matter more than the design of the moment. A design goes out of fashion; the gold does not. When a piece comes back to be remade, what carries forward is the metal.

It is worth thinking about that when buying. Ask what the piece weighs, ask its purity, and keep the bill.

posts.title: Reading a Hallmark Before You Buy
posts.excerpt: What the BIS mark actually tells you, and the two things worth checking on any gold purchase.
posts.body:
A BIS hallmark on gold jewellery records its purity — 22K, 18K, and so on — verified by an assaying centre rather than by the shop selling it.

Two things are worth doing on any purchase. Look for the mark on the piece itself, and keep the bill, which should state the weight, the purity and the making charges separately. Making charges are where two quotes for "the same" piece most often differ.

Ask. Any jeweller worth buying from will explain their figure without being pushed.

posts.title: Choosing a Gemstone the Sensible Way
posts.excerpt: Why the consultation should come before the purchase, not after.
posts.body:
People often buy a stone first and ask about it afterwards. It is worth doing in the other order.

A proper consultation covers which stone suits you, the weight it should be, the metal it should be set in and which finger it should be worn on. Those four answers change what you should buy — and sometimes the answer is a smaller stone than you were about to purchase.

We do the consultation before the sale for that reason. It is a better conversation when nobody has already paid for anything.
